methodological_questions: Does a teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR raise PNR PPP relative to matched PNRs without that preceding DRIVE?
Are play-type labels derived from the stats API play-by-play and the graph database reliable enough to define DRIVE and PNR possessions?
Do foul-ending and outcome-derived labels inflate PPP and bias the DRIVE-to-PNR contrast?
What sample sizes per sequence cell are needed, and are they available?

historical_evidence.finding: Play-type labeling audit found OTHER possessions with 36% foul endings and inflated PPP (FOUL_BUCKET); DRIVE was 12pp below the foul benchmark (FOUL_LEAK); PNR showed a 22% foul rate; only 335 of 50,668 possessions (0.7%) mapped to a real play type via initiation_type. Verdict recorded as artifact_found. Validation status: no_validation_recorded.

Sequential premium scan. Same-player and teammate X->Y sequences were ranked by PPP premium over Y's baseline. Recorded cells include L. Doncic DRIVE->PNR +0.309 (n=53) and D. Bane DRIVE->PNR -0.324 (n=70). Mechanism recorded as unclear; limited by label/classification error and small sample.

Season-stability test of top sequential suppressors across 30 stars x 4 seasons (min n=20 per cell). Only 2/30 (7%) met the 75% same-top-suppressor stability rule. Negative teammate cells included Giannis->Lillard DRIVE->PNR -0.263 (n=31). Mechanism recorded as B_powered_null. Validation status: no_validation_recorded.

Observed on-ball defensive scheme labelling (ORL-DET G1). Confident label rates were 14.9% (DET, 10 of 67) and 3.3% (ORL, 2 of 60). switches_on was not populated by the matchups feed. Verdict failed_gate. Not a direct test of DRIVE-to-PNR, but evidences label-coverage limits in this data.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Mapping possessions to play types via initiation_type and using PPP by play type as the basis for play-type efficiency claims.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as artifact: only 0.7% of possessions mapped to a real play type, and foul endings inflated OTHER PPP and shifted DRIVE and PNR PPP. The PPP differences reflected labelling and foul artifacts.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Ranking same-player and teammate X->Y sequence cells by PPP premium to find strong sequential effects.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as not a hypothesis test, with mechanism unclear and limits for label/classification error and small sample. Cell signs flip (e.g., DRIVE->PNR both positive and negative), so the scan does not yield a consistent effect.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing whether sequential suppressor premiums are stable across seasons.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as rejected by an adequately powered null: only 2/30 stars met the stability rule, and negative teammate cells were small (n about 31).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labelling on-ball defensive coverage from matchup and play-by-play fields.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as untestable (failed_gate): label rates were 3.3% to 14.9% and switches_on was unpopulated.

evidence_establishes: The derived play-type labels from initiation_type covered only about 0.7% of possessions in the audited set, so play-type labels as currently derived are not reliable for the question (FAM:SF-CHT-025).
Foul endings are common in PNR and DRIVE-adjacent possessions and can bias PPP-based comparisons (FAM:SF-CHT-025).
Prior sequence-premium scans found no stable teammate DRIVE->PNR effect; cell estimates were small-sample and sign-unstable (FAM:SF40, FAM:SF-APPA-058).
Label coverage limits recur across play-type and defensive-scheme work in this data (FAM:SF-APPS-058).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether a pooled teammate DRIVE-before-PNR contrast is positive. No returned record tests the pooled estimand with a validated label set and foul control.
Whether the current graph-database labels are the same as those audited in FAM:SF-CHT-025; the record does not say whether it used the current build.
The size of any true effect or the power of a pooled test. No record reports a pooled estimate with a confidence interval.
Results for the 2025-26 playoffs, which were partial at the question date (2026-06-14).
own_inferences: The question as posed (any teammate DRIVE preceding PNR raises PNR PPP) is a pooled claim about sequences, and its validity depends first on label validity.
Foul-ending and possession-attribution artifacts (FAM:SF-CHT-025) would bias a naive DRIVE->PNR PPP contrast upward or downward, so a naive comparison cannot be interpreted.
Sequence-cell scans (FAM:SF40, FAM:SF-APPA-058) imply a high multiple-comparisons risk if the question is answered by picking the best cell.
uncertainties: The records are truncated (cut in the retrieved text) and I did not read the full family records; full read_family text may change details.
The audit in FAM:SF-CHT-025 may predate the current graph build. Current label coverage is unknown.
The number of teammate DRIVE->PNR sequences in the 2022-23 to 2025-26 data is not reported.
Whether a teammate DRIVE before a PNR means the same team, the same possession, or the immediately preceding possession is not defined in the question.

historical_effect.explanation: Before retrieval, the plan was a standard sequence test with the derived labels. The retrieved records show that the derived play-type labels were recorded as an artifact source (0.7% coverage, foul-ending bias), that sequence scans of this kind were underpowered or unstable, and that a powered null occurred for stability. I therefore moved from proceed to do_not_proceed until the labels pass a validation gate. The question itself is not ruled out.

blocking_constraints.text: initiation_type mapped only 0.7% of possessions to a real play type in the audited set (FAM:SF-CHT-025); the DRIVE and PNR labels are not validated.
Labels derived from play-by-play may be defined using outcomes such as points or fouls, which makes the PPP outcome circular if the label is not independent of the result.
Shot quality, shooter and defender quality, lineup, and foul endings all confound a DRIVE->PNR PPP contrast.
Per-cell sequence samples are about 30 to 70 (FAM:SF40, FAM:SF-APPA-058), which is too small for a reliable pooled or cell-level test without a pre-specified pooled estimand.

prior_work.summary: No returned record tests the pooled teammate DRIVE-before-PNR PPP claim with validated labels. FAM:SF40 and FAM:SF-APPA-058 touch on DRIVE->PNR cells with small, sign-unstable estimates and no pooled test. FAM:SF-CHT-025 shows the labels used to define the play types are unreliable. Prior work partly addresses related issues but does not answer the question as posed.

risks.text: The teammate DRIVE and PNR labels may be mis-assigned, given 0.7% initiation_type coverage (FAM:SF-CHT-025).
Labels defined using points or foul outcomes would make the PPP contrast partly circular.
Shot quality, player quality, lineup, and foul endings confound the sequence effect.
Sequence-cell sample sizes near n=30 to 70 give wide intervals (FAM:SF40, FAM:SF-APPA-058).
Scanning many player and teammate sequence cells and reporting the best ones inflates false positives (FAM:SF40).
Without a placebo sequence check, any PPP difference may reflect possession-type or foul-ending structure rather than a drive effect.
Four seasons plus playoffs mix rule and style changes; season-to-season instability was recorded (FAM:SF-APPA-058).
Defensive-matchup and scheme labels are sparse and partly unpopulated (FAM:SF-APPS-058), so matchup controls are unreliable.
Cross-source joins between the graph database and per-game files may misalign possessions; no reconciliation is recorded.

design.estimand: Gate first: the label-validity estimand is the agreement rate between derived DRIVE and PNR labels and a manually audited sample. Only if that passes, the primary estimand is the within-team difference in PNR PPP (teammate-initiated PNR possessions) preceded by a teammate DRIVE possession versus preceded by a non-DRIVE possession, adjusted for controls.
design.unit: Possession (PNR possession), with the preceding possession as the sequence context; team-game as a clustering level.
design.sample: Regular seasons 2022-23 to 2024-25 and 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13). Exclude 2025-26 playoffs, which were partial at 2026-06-14. Exclude fouled and non-shot-ending possessions as a sensitivity analysis.
design.power: Pre-specify minimum detectable effect before analysis from the pooled possession count after label validation. Not computed here; no pooled count is available in the records.
design.controls: Shooter and defender quality (player fixed effects or prior-season PPP), lineup, shot distance and type, foul-ending indicator, clock and score state, and defensive matchup where populated. Use team-game and player fixed effects.
design.falsification: Placebo sequences: a teammate non-DRIVE action (e.g., SPOT_UP or POST_UP) before PNR, and a DRIVE after the PNR. Expect null on both. Also check that the effect is absent when labels are randomly permuted within team-game.
design.multiplicity: One pre-specified pooled contrast as primary. All cell-level sequence results are exploratory and reported with false-discovery-rate control.
design.decision_rule: Proceed to the substantive test only if label validation agreement passes a pre-set threshold and the placebo checks are null. Call the effect supported only if the pooled primary contrast is positive with a 95% CI excluding zero and the placebo checks hold. Otherwise report rejected (if powered), artifact (if placebo or foul sensitivity removes the effect), or uncertain.
design.data_version: Data available as of 2026-06-14: 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs, 2025-26 regular season (complete), and 2025-26 playoffs excluded (partial at that date). Record the graph-database build version and reconcile it against the audited build in FAM:SF-CHT-025.

methodological_questions: Does a teammate drive before a pick-and-roll raise PNR points per possession?
How reliable are play-type labels derived from NBA stats API play-by-play action and sub-type fields?
What confounders (shot quality, player quality, lineup, sample size) threaten estimating the drive-to-PNR effect?
Could derived labels or outcome-based definitions cause leakage or circularity?
args.query: teammate drive preceding pick-and-roll effect on PNR possession points PPP play-type labeling data quality NBA play-by-play

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 4 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-06-14, in the area of play-type labeling and data quality):
Any teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR raises PNR PPP.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
